action.message:
Propose CAP-Distill (Client-Adaptive Private Representation Distillation): clients retain private heads while collaboratively training a shared backbone. Local loss combines supervision, global-teacher representation/logit distillation, and a proximal term. A bounded, DP-noised client shift/uncertainty score—based on entropy, calibration, and representation drift—controls each client’s personalization bound and learning rate: high-shift clients receive more head adaptation and smaller shared-backbone steps; stable clients receive stronger global transfer. Clip updates to adaptive bounds, add Gaussian noise, and use secure aggregation. Report client-level DP using RDP accounting with q, sigma, T, and delta.

Novelty: existing FedProx/Moreau, Ditto, FedPer/FedRep, hypernetworks, and self-distillation methods generally do not jointly provide adaptive DP, fairness, robustness, and interpretable client adaptation; fixed-noise DP methods waste utility under heterogeneity. The method exposes an adaptation certificate via each client’s shift score, bound, and effective learning rate.

Challenges: adaptive clipping can leak distribution information; noisy uncertainty estimates can misallocate personalization; teacher bias, DP noise, minority classes, dropout, and aggregation heterogeneity can hurt performance. Safeguards include bounded [Cmin,Cmax] parameters, EMA smoothing, DP/noised public bins, minimum participation, robust aggregation, and dropout sensitivity analysis.

Evaluate CIFAR-10/100 and FEMNIST under Dirichlet label skew (alpha 0.1/0.5) and quantity skew with 50/100 clients and partial participation; optionally Shakespeare. Baselines: FedAvg, FedProx, pFedMe, Ditto, FedPer, FedRep, DP-FedAvg, and DP-pFedMe. Ablate distillation, fixed versus adaptive bounds, entropy versus drift scores, private versus nonprivate scores, head/backbone split, privacy noise, distillation weight, dropout, and noisy labels. Metrics: mean/median and worst-10% accuracy, macro-F1, 90th–10th percentile fairness gap, ECE, membership-inference leakage, epsilon/delta, communication bytes, convergence rounds, and robustness. Expected result: at matched epsilon, improved mean and worst-client accuracy, reduced fairness gap, and interpretable score-performance correlation. Search evidence: Wang et al., “Differential Privacy Personalized Federated Learning Based on Dynamically Sparsified Client Updates,” arXiv:2503.09192, reports adaptive norm/sparsification but leaves broader adaptive personalization and transparent fairness analysis open.

Technical contribution: define private client shift and uncertainty scores locally, transmitting only clipped DP-noised scalars via secure aggregation. Set eta_i = eta_min + (eta_max-eta_min)sigmoid(a*s_i - b*u_i), with EMA smoothing and server-enforced bounds; high shift permits adaptation while high uncertainty suppresses unstable updates. Train with task loss plus proximal anchoring and global-backbone representation/logit distillation. Clip updates/statistics, use robust trimmed/median aggregation, trust-region checks, dropout fallback, and RDP accounting. Evaluate on CIFAR-10/100 with Dirichlet label/quantity skew and FEMNIST, comparing FedAvg, FedProx, Ditto, pFedMe, FedPer, and FedRep. Measure mean, worst-client and 10th-percentile accuracy, fairness gap, ECE, convergence, communication, privacy epsilon, and robustness. Ablate dynamic versus fixed bounds, shift/uncertainty signals, distillation, DP noise, robust aggregation, heterogeneity, and personalization strength. Risks include noisy small-client estimates, miscalibration, poisoned signals, dropout, overhead, and privacy–utility trade-offs. Prior methods generally personalize with fixed coefficients or architectures but do not jointly provide DP-protected adaptive strength, fairness, robustness, and interpretable adaptation traces.

Uploaded experimental plan with datasets, partitions, baselines, metrics, ablations, and risks. Artifact ID: f02b994efc8f4b1ca9898a61638d673e. Key evaluation: CIFAR-10/100 Dirichlet and quantity skew, FEMNIST natural skew; FedAvg/FedProx/Ditto/FedPer/FedRep/pFedMe; mean and worst-client accuracy, fairness gap, communication, convergence, robustness, and DP utility curves; adaptive-bound and uncertainty-signal ablations.

Propose Private Adaptive Representation Distillation (PARD-FL): combine client-level differential privacy, uncertainty/support/disagreement-based adaptive personalization bounds, persistent private heads, and interpretable adaptation reports. Compare FedPer, FedRep, Ditto, pFedMe, and distillation baselines. Evaluate mean and worst-client accuracy, fairness gap, calibration, privacy leakage, robustness, convergence, and communication cost on CIFAR-10/100 and FEMNIST under label, quantity, and covariate skew. Existing methods do not jointly provide formal privacy, fairness, robust adaptation, and transparent client-level explanations. Key risks include DP noise, noisy estimates, teacher bias, client dropout, and overhead; mitigate with EMA estimates, bound clipping, minimum-support shrinkage, robust aggregation, and privacy accounting.
